findings.title: Root-wide write failures are incorrectly contained
findings.evidence: crates/blit-core/src/remote/transfer/sink.rs:140-146 treats any existing directory as a live destination root, and :157-165 therefore converts errors such as EROFS into a per-file outcome; crates/blit-core/src/transfer_session/mod.rs:4633-4650 makes those outcomes fatal only for non-mirror sessions.
findings.predicted_failure: A mirror targeting an existing read-only mount can contain every failed write, transfer no files, and still return a successful summary when there are no extraneous entries to delete. This silently leaves the backup incomplete, justifying HIGH severity.
findings.better_approach: Keep root-wide errors such as ReadOnlyFilesystem fatal before constructing SinkOutcome::failed, with a read-only-root regression test.

findings.title: Push progress still reports destination-failed files complete
findings.evidence: crates/blit-core/src/remote/transfer/pipeline.rs:509-521 filters against the local sink outcome, but DataPlaneSink returns SinkOutcome::written immediately after transmission at crates/blit-core/src/remote/transfer/sink.rs:1227-1236; the in-stream sender likewise emits FileComplete unconditionally at crates/blit-core/src/transfer_session/mod.rs:2962-2967 and :3150-3155. Pushes wire this source-side progress at crates/blit-core/src/remote/transfer/session_client.rs:199-200.
findings.predicted_failure: For an initiator-SOURCE mirror, a destination open, flush, or metadata failure is contained after the sender has emitted FileComplete. CLI verbose/JSON progress consequently identifies a file as completed and increments completed-file totals even though it is absent or incomplete at the destination, an observable correctness error warranting MEDIUM severity.
findings.better_approach: Emit FileComplete only from destination-confirmed outcomes, or delay source-side completions until the returned failure report can filter failed paths.
